Listen to this article Share United Nigeria Airlines will begin scheduled flight operations linking Jos, the Plateau State capital, with Lagos, Kano and Owerri, giving residents of the state three new connections. The operations will start on November 24, and tickets are already available for purchase. Advertisement Advertisement The Lagos–Jos–Lagos operations will be the most frequent of the three, with four flights each week on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. The Jos–Kano–Jos route will operate twice a week, on Tuesdays and Fridays, while the Jos–Owerri–Jos route will also run twice weekly, on Wednesdays and Sundays. Read also: British Airways seeks more Nigeria flights as FG considers BASA review Because the Owerri airport is currently closed, the first Jos–Owerri flight will depart on Sunday, November 29, 2026, five days after the general start date. On Monday, November 9, the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, United Nigeria Airlines will introduce scheduled flights on two routes the state had not previously been served on: Jos–Kano in the North-West and Jos–Owerri in the South-East. Advertisement Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership forms part of the state’s broader effort to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunity. He thanked the airline’s management for their confidence in the state’s vision. The commissioner said the Jos–Owerri route would make it easier for residents of Plateau and neighbouring states to reach the South-East and South-South, supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchange in those regions. He said the Jos–Kano route would deepen Plateau’s ties with the North-West, which he described as home to some of the country’s major commercial and industrial centres and said offers significant opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Advertisement Read also: Nigeria seeks direct flights to Ireland, sets up team for BASA review Responding on behalf of United Nigeria Airlines, Mazi Osita, Managing Director, Okonkwo, said the agreement stands out because it connects the South-East, South-West and North-Central zones. He described Plateau as a special and strategic state and said the airline intends to meet the standard of service for which it is known. Advertisement Advertisement Okonkwo also thanked Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, and commended the commissioner for his efforts in bringing the deal to completion. Passengers can book tickets through United Nigeria Airlines’ website, flyunitednigeria.com, its mobile app, or accredited travel agents. She is also the Deputy Editor, BusinessDay Weekender Magazine, the Saturday Weekend edition of BusinessDay. She holds a BSC in Mass Communication from the prestigious University of Nigeria, Nsukka and a Masters degree in Marketing at the University of Lagos. As the lead writer on the aviation desk, Ifeoma is responsible and in charge of the three weekly aviation and travel pages in BusinessDay and BDSunday. She also overseas and edits all pages of BusinessDay Saturday Weekender. She has written various investigative, features and news stories in aviation and business related issues and has been severally nominated for award in the category of Aviation Writer of the Year by the Nigeria Media Nite-Out awards; one of the Nigeria’s most prestigious media awards ceremonies. Ifeoma is a one-time winner of the prestigious Nigeria Media Merit Award under the 'Aviation Writer of the Year' Category. She is the 2025 Eloy Award winner under the Print Media Journalist category. She has undergone several journalism trainings by various prestigious organisations. Ifeoma is also a fellow of the Female Reporters Leadership Fellowship of the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism.
